# 2026-10-22 — memory + speed snapshot vs reference codecs

Post-v1-cleanup build (working tree). One file, one run each — quick
orientation, not a tuned benchmark. Input: 73.6 MiB i16 stereo 48 kHz WAV
(dense wind recording; every codec lands ~63%, so this file sits in the
hard-to-compress tail of the corpus).

Method: `mem_bench.py` (in `D:\TEMP\flq_ab`) — `GetProcessMemoryInfo`
`PeakWorkingSetSize` polled on the child process handle every ~1 ms; wall
time via `perf_counter`. Peak RSS ≠ counted heap (includes loader +
runtime baseline ~3–4 MiB); thread counts differ per tool
(flq 24 cores, flac -j8, ape -threads=4, wavpack/ofr/tak 1-thread CLI).

| tool | out % src | enc s | enc peak MiB | dec s | dec peak MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **flq** | 63.4% | 1.50 | 38.5 | 1.30 | 4.9 |
| flac -8 -j8 | 63.4% | 0.23 | 20.7 | 0.43 | 4.5 |
| wavpack -hx | 63.1% | 1.39 | 13.7 | 0.37 | 10.5 |
| ofr extranew-light | 62.4% | 12.28 | 13.1 | 9.15 | 4.2 |
| tak -p4m | 62.9% | 2.12 | 8.6 | 0.58 | 8.4 |
| ape -c4000 | 62.9% | 0.64 | 22.5 | 0.72 | 13.0 |

Reads:

- **Decode memory is table stakes, and flq meets it**: 4.9 MiB process
  peak vs 4.2–13.0 MiB across the field (internal counted heap is
  ~0.6 MiB — the rest is process/runtime baseline). This is the v3 → v1
  fix: the old whole-file archive needed ~1.6 GiB here.
- **Encode memory**: flq is heaviest (38.5 MiB) but within 2× of flac;
  parallel frame buffers + runtime baseline.
- **Encode speed**: flq 49 MiB/s vs flac ~320 MiB/s (-j8) — ~6.5× slower;
  faster than tak -p4m here, far faster than ofr.
- **Decode speed**: flq ~3× slower than flac/wavpack — that row predates
  parallel frame decode; see the scaling sweep below.

## Scaling sweep (same day, `memtime.py`)

Generated i16 stereo 48 kHz WAVs (0.5/2/5/10 min ≈ 5.5/22/55/110 MiB),
one run per cell, same machine (i7-14650HX, 24 threads; flq default
`-j` = all cores for encode and decode).

| input | tool | enc s | enc peak MiB | dec s | dec peak MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 min / 5.5 MiB | **flq** | 0.31 | 36.4 | 0.05 | 22.6 |
| | flac -8 -j8 | 0.03 | 14.8 | 0.07 | 4.5 |
| | wavpack -hx | 0.12 | 13.6 | 0.04 | 10.5 |
| | tak -p4m | 0.19 | 8.6 | 0.06 | 8.4 |
| 2 min / 22 MiB | **flq** | 1.17 | 38.8 | 0.20 | 27.3 |
| | flac -8 -j8 | 0.09 | 20.9 | 0.17 | 4.5 |
| | wavpack -hx | 0.42 | 13.7 | 0.11 | 10.5 |
| | tak -p4m | 0.67 | 8.6 | 0.19 | 8.4 |
| 5 min / 55 MiB | **flq** | 2.93 | 39.2 | 0.44 | 27.3 |
| | flac -8 -j8 | 0.16 | 20.4 | 0.33 | 4.5 |
| | wavpack -hx | 1.02 | 13.7 | 0.28 | 10.5 |
| | tak -p4m | 1.65 | 8.6 | 0.47 | 8.4 |
| 10 min / 110 MiB | **flq** | 5.93 | 39.8 | 0.87 | 27.8 |
| | flac -8 -j8 | 0.31 | 20.9 | 0.64 | 4.5 |
| | wavpack -hx | 2.04 | 13.9 | 0.55 | 10.5 |
| | tak -p4m | 3.32 | 8.6 | 0.96 | 8.4 |

Reads:

- Memory is **flat in input length for every tool** — all stream. flq
  enc ~40 MiB (~2× flac), dec ~28 MiB (24 worker threads' stacks +
  runtime baseline; counted heap stays ~0.6 MiB).
- flq encode ~19× flac -8 -j8 wall at 10 min (5.93 s vs 0.31 s) —
  ~100× realtime; between wavpack -hx and tak -p4m.
- flq decode is on par with the field now: 0.87 s vs flac 0.64 /
  wavpack 0.55 / tak 0.96 on the 10-minute file.
